lines: When a whale dies, it sinks to the bottom of the ocean with about 30 tons of carbon dioxide inside its body.
This carbon stays deep in the ocean for a long time.
One tree takes in only about 22 kilograms of carbon dioxide each year, so one whale is equal to thousands of trees.
Whales also help the ocean in another way.
Their waste becomes food for tiny plants called phytoplankton.
These tiny plants also remove carbon from the air.
That’s why scientists call whales “Earth’s protectors.”
In 2019, some experts said, “Every whale is worth more than two million dollars because it helps nature so much.
But many whales were hunted in the past, and their number decreased.”
A plan is needed to protect whales.
They can be a key to slowing down climate change.
